agreement.description: Logix and Digital Research agree to develop a new CP/M version for Logix Aurelia. DRI fully owns the resulting CP/M version and makes it available to other vendors through non-exclusive licensing. The collaboration adds a text-mode TUI, smart-device and card integration, XIP cartridge support and named user areas.

clauses.statement: DRI retains the right to implement the TUI libraries and FlexiBUS support in CP/M versions for non-Logix computers.

Logix supplies Aurelia platform requirements, interface knowledge and integration work; DRI develops and integrates the CP/M operating-system changes. They cooperate on interoperability and qualification for Aurelia. Hardware, devices and cards remain platform deliverables rather than DRI hardware-manufacturing obligations.

DRI fully owns the new CP/M version and its CP/M software enhancements developed through this collaboration. DRI may offer and license that version to any other vendor on non-exclusive terms. Aurelia compatibility and Logix collaboration confer no exclusive CP/M distribution right on Logix. Hardware and technology ownership are not transferred by this software-ownership term.

Provide a text-mode TUI: pseudo-window interfaces, menus and shared interaction conventions that make applications usable through a consistent text-screen interface. Integrate the Logix TUI standard with CP/M software services.
Support smart devices and expansion cards using Plug and Execute and FlexiBUS technologies, with documented CP/M integration so qualified devices and cards can expose their functions to applications.
Support XIP cartridges and their software interfaces so suitable programs can execute in place from cartridge ROM on compatible hardware.

Allow names to be assigned to CP/M file User Numbers, presenting user areas as named directory-like locations. This supplies a named organisation layer over User Numbers without asserting a new hierarchical filesystem.

agreement.description: BPI Systems accepts Adam’s $150,000 investment in exchange for a 33% fully diluted interest. The agreement obliges AION Software to provide knowledge and resources to refactor BPI’s existing code into C with a competitive text-mode TUI. Further investment supports ports to future systems and platforms, after which BPI has the right to buy back Adam’s shares.

clauses.statement: Adam agrees to subscribe $150,000 of new capital into BPI Systems for development and working capital. BPI accepts the subscription; it is company funding rather than a payment to existing owners.

The accepted investment agreement allocates Adam a 33% fully diluted interest in BPI Systems in exchange for his $150,000 subscription. Existing owners retain the remaining 67%, subject to the agreed later buyback right.

AION Software must provide the knowledge, engineering resources and development assistance needed to refactor BPI’s current code into C and deliver a competitive TUI with pseudo-window interaction in text mode. BPI retains ownership of its applications and its independent brand and management.

The cooperation includes further investment and engineering work to port the refactored BPI software to future systems and platforms. AION Software supplies the associated technical knowledge and resources. Additional funding amounts, allocation among contributors, target platforms and schedules remain unspecified.

Following the agreed redevelopment and subsequent porting work, BPI Systems may buy back Adam’s shares. This is BPI’s right, not an automatic transfer or a mandatory buyback. The agreement does not specify a price, valuation formula, exercise date or payment schedule.
